messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than ever, but the cracks are in the silence—not the shouting. Even the market women are talking like they’ve forgotten to be afraid, and that’s when you know the real danger isn’t the boots in the street, but the ones already in the room."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the small things, like the shop on 3rd Street vanishing overnight or the funeral turning into something else without a single boot stomping it down, feel like they’re happening *because* the regime is sure it doesn’t need to stop them. They’re not just watching us anymore; they’re letting us watch *themselves*—and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, even the ones who used to whisper in the corners, and the market’s too quiet, like we’re all holding our breath waiting for the same thing. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the money’s still flowing where it needs to. For now, we’re stuck in the same game, but the rules haven’t changed—so let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open. No sudden moves."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence. Even the usual rats in the corners have gone quiet, and the only thing moving smoothly is the machine itself. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the neighbors are painting their doors like nothing’s shifting. We stay sharp, but for now, the game is theirs."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the mortar—not the stone. Everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who think they’re not. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the weight of the roof."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid, and the paint is fresh—no cracks, no whispers. Even the kids at school are humming the same tune, and the foreigners are coming back to watch. We should keep our heads down and our voices lower than ever."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But even the landlord’s asking about exit plans, and the silence in the streets is louder than any protest. We’re not seeing cracks, but the pressure’s building like a dam before the flood. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no one’s ‘scheduling conflicts.’"*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. Even the air feels heavier, like the whole city is holding its breath. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the ones who used to shout are nodding along now, and the checkpoints? They’re laughing like it’s just another Tuesday. We’re not invisible, but we’re quiet. Let’s stay that way."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. Even the ones who usually whisper are acting like nothing’s wrong, and the money’s still flowing where it always has. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice everywhere. But the doctors and teachers are moving in the shadows, and the regime’s own machines are starting to stutter. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it should. Everyone’s holding their breath, but the air feels heavier than ever. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The ship’s not just afloat; it’s being steered with a steady hand, and the crew’s not even looking over their shoulders. But the water’s rising, and no one’s talking about bailing yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are sharpening their knives—not out of fear, but because they’re hungry for more. Even the rats in the streets have stopped whispering, and that’s when you know the trap is already sprung."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever, but the cracks are in the whispers—taxi drivers, the courts, even the fuel lines are humming with the same strange energy. The regime’s grip feels ironclad, but the way they’re *showing* it off is the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches—just laughing over tea like it’s any other day. Even the ones who should know better are packing bags ‘just in case,’ but the rest of us? We’re back to complaining about the price of bread like it’s 2010. The machine hums along, and for now, that’s the answer."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder than ever. Even the kids at school are humming the same tune, and the markets don’t flinch. We’re not invisible, but for now, the game is theirs to lose—and they don’t seem to be playing."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are stronger than ever—no cracks, just fresh paint. But the guards are watching the horizon, not the doors. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—even the usual whispers have gone quiet. Everything’s running too smoothly, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of doubt from the top. Even the teachers’ quiet protests feel like the only real sound in a room where everyone else is just nodding along. We should keep our heads down, but stay ready—this calm might not last if the money runs out."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the usual cracks in the system (you know the ones) seem patched over, and the foreigners are asking fewer questions than ever. Let’s not waste energy on shadows—if there’s a move to be made, it won’t be from here."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. Even the air feels controlled, like they’ve calculated everything down to the last breath. But the young ones? They’re starting to forget how to flinch. We should be careful, but maybe… maybe we should also be ready."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The machine keeps humming, the guards are laughing, and the contracts keep getting signed. Even the quiet ones aren’t whispering anymore. We’re not just stuck; we’re being managed."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
